productDefects.observed: After the destination returned, nothing was delivered: every lease and acknowledgement failed with SQLITE_FULL (log 1002 repeated). Linux: 26,374 queued, 0 delivered for 15 minutes. Windows: 2,500 delivered in 25 minutes.
productDefects.cause: Intake and settlement shared one page ceiling (cap + 4 MiB); intake filled it and settlement enlarges rows.

productDefects.observed: WAL 72.6 MB beside a 71.3 MB database exceeded the pre-write budget (about 140 MB for a 64 MiB cap), refusing every write including acknowledgements; background retention failed (log 3001 x49).
productDefects.fix: 131b37e (truncate checkpoint before refusing a write, at most every 10 s).

productDefects.observed: After 22,516 events drained, pages were 99.95% of the intake limit, all fresh acknowledgements; the retention floor kept them, so intake stayed refused.
productDefects.fix: 131b37e (reclaim acknowledged rows of any age once intake is blocked).

productDefects.observed: 21,494 sequence numbers (ws3l0033667-ws3l0055160) handed to TCP by rsyslog but not yet read by Bower were lost when the collector restarted while backpressured; rsyslog counted them processed. Destination: 33,666 distinct, 3,992 duplicate rows (replays after ambiguous acknowledgements during the stall).
productDefects.cause: Plain syslog over TCP has no application acknowledgement; kernel socket buffers held about 4 MB.
productDefects.fix: Not a queue defect. The drain fix removes the need for the restart; RELP (merged separately, #168) withholds acknowledgements. Documented.

harnessFailures.observed: Linux queue-cap attempt 1 stopped after 30 s: the one-line nftables rule needed separators. 3,306 sequence numbers were generated and later delivered normally.

After mounting the queue volume at the state folder, ACLs set on the mount point applied to the reparse point; the service could not write the WAL and hung at start (SCM 7009). A recursive icacls /inheritance:r /T then left queue files with empty ACLs; repaired with takeown and icacls /reset. No data was lost. Documented in the Windows procedure.
Linux watermarks attempt 1: growing one preallocated filler by about 700 MB failed on xfs after the warning stage. Fixed with bounded 64 MiB chunks.

Windows queue-cap and watermarks summaries failed (Measure-Object on hashtable rows). The queue-cap journal was recovered and summarised offline (wec-queue-cap-runs.json); the watermarks journal was lost with the host. Windows watermarks are therefore proven only in run bower-ws3b.
Linux disk-full stopped when closing the filler raised ENOSPC; the run was not completed. Proven in run bower-ws3b.
A unit test redirecting the WAL to /dev/full failed in CI with SQLITE_CANTOPEN; replaced by portable page-limit and restart-while-critical tests. Real ENOSPC is proven on AWS volumes.
